The later autonomy campaign superseded PVE34 as an operating prescription—not as historical evidence—by proving clean >1k/sec alpha parsing, adaptive fetch behavior, scenario-specific DB rebalancing, and parser-owned S3 throughput above 2k/sec. The result established PVE34 as the local fixed-profile keeper for that band and showed substantial idle headroom because DB/write coordination—not fetch or JSON—was limiting throughput; it did not establish PVE34 as a universal autonomous policy.

Separately, make the raid profile route render local raid results first and defer Bungie collectible enrichment and unopened Pantheon work. claims.value: The highest-value non-profile target is the `/in/playerActivity` cache-miss path. Seven-day RUM recorded 13,210 calls with avg 3.69 s, p75 1.09 s, and p95 12.03 s; seven-day APM recorded 23,255 exact `GET /in/playerActivity` spans with avg 1.99 s, p75 2 ms, and p95 13.03 s. The sharp 2 ms p75 versus 13.03 s p95 identifies cache misses as the damaging tail, while the last 24h logs recorded 68 foreground rebuilds and 204 shard logs, with shard-scan p95 about 18 s and math p95 about 16 s. It also affects the high-traffic analytics home fan-out: `analytics.home` had 9,770 initial views, p75 load 3.41 s, p75 LCP 3.03 s, and `/in/playerActivity` was among its top API resources.

Proposed intervention: make `/in/playerActivity` stale-while-revalidate. Preserve a longer-lived stale value, refresh it in the background under a single refresh/distributed lock, and never let ordinary web requests perform the Redis shard scan and math rebuild. The code-path reason is that `apiPlayerActivity` first reads the `apiPlayerActivity` cache but falls back synchronously to `memcache.GetPlayerActivity`; meanwhile `sweeperbot.cachePlayerActivity` writes every 5 minutes with a matching 5 minute TTL, leaving misses or refresh gaps able to push expensive rebuild work into foreground requests. On refresh failure, continue serving the last stale value; if no value has ever been built, return an explicit unavailable/no-data response instead of rebuilding synchronously, matching the documented Discord behavior.

On `/p/:identifier/raids`, remove Bungie collectibles and speculative Pantheon loading from the first-render critical path. `loadLogbookRaidSources` waits for every concurrent source, but local raid sources were only milliseconds (`raiddifficultysummaries` avg/95th about 2.7 ms, `raidcarries` avg about 6.1 ms and 95th about 10.1 ms, `raidseals` avg/95th about 0.6 ms), whereas `bungie.GetD2ProfileStats(..., bungie.ProfileWCollectibles)` was the slow source (`bungieprofile` avg about 2.70 s and 95th about 3.77 s). Change the route to render a ready scaffold plus clears/full clears/carries/fastest from the shell and fast local sources, then fetch collectible/progress enrichment asynchronously; lazy-load Pantheon only when selected, or share/cache one server-side `ProfileWCollectibles` result. Images are secondary—their p95 was 264 ms, not the 3–4 s blocker.

It must preserve not only learned knowledge but the live, inspectable state needed to resume and advance complex work. Obsidian is a prototype corpus and human-readable projection—not the canonical product, storage, or interaction boundary.
